Purpose and Scope
Article 1 - The purpose of this directive is to regulate the matters regarding the staff and students from Gebze Technical
University who will go to the higher education institutions and enterprises included in the program for education and
teaching within the scope of the Erasmus+ Program.
Definitions
Article 2 - The following terms in this Directive have the following meanings:
University : Gebze Technical University
Division : Faculty, Institute, Department, Administrative Division
Commission : Commission for the selection of students and staff to benefit from Erasmus+ exchange
Erasmus : Higher education-related sub-program of the Erasmus+ Program
National Agency : Center for European Union Education and Youth Programs
Inter-Institutional Agreement: Student / staff exchange agreement between the university’s divisions and the divisions
of the universities included in Erasmus+
Learning Agreement:
a) An agreement signed by the student himself/herself and the Departmental and/or Institutional Erasmus Coordinators
of both higher education institutions, including the university the student will attend, the courses he/she will take and
the credits of these courses for study mobility
b) For traineeship mobility, an agreement signed by GTU’s Departmental and/or Institutional Erasmus Coordinators
and the host institution, which expresses the nature of the traineeship and includes student information
Erasmus Student Charter: The document given to the Erasmus exchange student before leaving the University, stating
the rights and obligations of the student
Coordination Office: Gebze Technical University Institutional Erasmus Coordination Office
Departmental Coordination Office: Gebze Technical University Departmental Erasmus Coordination Office
REQUIREMENTS FOR EXCHANGE
Article 3-
3.1. In order to be able to carry out student and staff teaching mobility within the scope of Erasmus+ Program, an inter-
institutional agreement must be made and the agreement must be submitted to the Coordination Office before the
application announcement date determined for the student / staff selection process. There is no inter -institutional
agreement requirement for student traineeship and staff training mobility.
If the higher education institution wishes, it may modify the format of the inter-institutional agreement to also include
its traineeship and staff training activities and settle the related matters in the agreement.
3.2. The project budget is allocated for the activities carried out on the dates specified in the "Erasmus+ Program Guide”
prepared by the Center for European Union Education and Youth Programs for each project period.
Article 4 -
4.1. The student must be a full-time student enrolled in a higher education program (Undergraduate / Master's / Doctoral)
at any of the formal education levels within the higher education institution and have a sufficient number of ECTS credit
load. English preparatory class students cannot apply. The mobility of new graduates is organized by the Coordination
Office with the approval of the Rectorate.
4.2. The minimum GPA to be accepted for undergraduate and graduate students who will apply to the program is
determined and announced according to the average specified in the "Erasmus Program Guide" prepared by the Center
for European Union Education and Youth Programs for each project period.
4.3. Students/staff apply to the Erasmus Coordination Office between the dates determined and announced by the Office.
The applications must include the details and approval of the academic advisor and departmental coordinator for the
student and the head of the department/division for the staff.

4.4. The student must score at least 70 out of 100 points in the foreign language exam conducted by GTU Department
of Foreign Languages or an equivalent score of 70 from an exam conducted by ÖSYM and accepted as equivalent. The
exam results are valid for the periods accepted by the University Senate.
4.5. The rights of the student/staff who was selected in the previous project period, but could not be sent due to lack of
grants or other reasons cannot be transferred to the next project as a "vested right". Students/staff to participate in the
program are re-evaluated and selected in each agreement period.
4.6. Academic or administrative staff who wish to participate in the mobility to teach or receive training abroad must be
full/part-time employed academic or administrative staff who are actually working in the institution.
4.7. In teaching and study mobility, the duration of the activity is determined as minimum 2 (two) working days and
maximum 2 (two) months excluding travel. In teaching mobility, 8 (eight) hours of activity minimum must be carried
out weekly. The Erasmus Coordination Office may set a different maximum period, provided that it is announced before
the student and staff selections.
EVALUATION OF APPLICATIONS
Article 5-
5.1. Applications are evaluated by a commission consisting of at least 3 people with an odd number of members under
the chairpersonhip of the Institutional Erasmus Coordinator appointed by the Rectorate.
5.2. The Commission is responsible for ensuring that the evaluation of applications is carried out in a transparent and
impartial manner.
5.3. The Commission evaluates student and staff applications according to the selection criteria in the "Erasmus Program
Guide" prepared by the Center for European Union Education and Youth Programs for each project period.
5.4. The results of the evaluation are announced on the relevant web pages and department bulletin boards, including
the scores received by all students and staff applying to the Erasmus+ program and the lists of full/alternate candidates.
5.5. After the results of the evaluation are announced, students are given a period of time to confirm their placement at
the university they have been placed or to give up their right. This period is announced in the application announcement.
The student who d oes not confirm that he/she will go to the university he/she has earned the right to go within the
specified period of time is considered to have given up his/her right and the reserve student waiting in the first place is
placed in his/her place.
5.6. Repealed.
5.7. The minimum language scores that academic and administrative staff who will benefit from Erasmus+ Staff
Mobility must obtain from a foreign language exam are as follows:
1. Teaching Mobility:
- Faculty Members/Academic Teaching Staff: 80 (YDS or equivalent)
2. Study Mobility:
- For Language Education for Faculty Members/Academic Staff: 65 (YDS or equivalent)
- For Certified Vocational Training for Faculty Members/Academic Staff: 80 (YDS or equivalent)
- For Administrative Staff: 50 (The result of the exam conducted by GTU Department of Foreign Languages or
the result of the exam conducted by ÖSYM may be used.)
MOBILITY PROCESSES FOR THOSE WHOSE APPLICATIONS ARE ACCEPTED
Article 6 -
6.1. Students may study and/or serve traineeships abroad within the scope of the program in accordance with the
minimum and maximum periods set by the European Commission.
6.2. The courses that the student will take at the host institution do not have to have the same titles as the courses that
the student is obliged to take in the relevant semester/year at our University, but the courses that are closest in content
and equivalent in hours/weeks/credits must be selected with the knowledge and approval of the Departmental Erasmus
Coordinator and Academic Advisor. In accordance with the National Agency's Program Guide, it is recommended that

students take 30 ECTS equivalent courses in one semester. The courses in the learning agreement of undergraduate and
graduate students who will go within the scope of the program are determined and approved by the advisor and the
Erasmus coordinator of the relevant department, and the courses selected are decided by the relevant Faculty Executive
Board, and the courses of graduate students are decided by the relevant Graduate School Executive Board and notified
to the Directorate of Student Affairs and Erasmus Coordinator.
6.3. If the student has to change the courses in his/her study abroad agreement after he/she starts studying abroad, he/she
must immediately notify the Erasmus Coordination Office and the Erasmus coordinators of the relevant departments
both at the institution he/she is attending and at GTU. The changes must be approved by the relevant department and
faculty/institute executive boards through the procedure described in Article 6.2 and the result must be notified to the
Directorate of Student Affairs . Course changes that are not approved by the relevant executive boards will not be
recognized upon the student’s return to GTU and will affect Erasmus+ grant payments in accordance with program
rules.
6.4. The outgoing students/staff within the scope of the program are paid from the budget allocated to the Coordination
Office on the dates, amounts and procedures determined by the National Agency for each project period. 80% of the
total grant amount is paid before the mobility. The remaining grant amount is calculated based on the certificate of
participation submitted upon return.
6.5. The grant is paid in Euros through the Coordination Office without any deductions (tax, social security and/or other
social costs, administrative management or registration fee).
6.6. In the event that the student/staff member leaves his/her mobility abroad for any reason, fails to complete his/her
studies, or fails t o be successful in at least two -thirds of the course program specified in the learning agreement, the
right to partially or fully withhold the remaining payment , or to request the return of the payment already made , is
reserved. However, 20% of the total grant calculated for the period of stay abroad will not be paid under any
circumstances if the student or staff membe r does not continue the planned activity during their time abroad, is found
to have failed to fulfill their obligations, or completely fails the courses or activities they attended.
6.7. Each student/staff member shall sign a grant agreement with the Coordination Office before receiving an exchange
grant. The grant agreement is signed by the Institutional Erasmus Coordinator on behalf of the Legal Representative of
the Institution.
6.8. Students who will go within the scope of the exchange program are given an Erasmus Student Charter before leaving
the university. This charter specifies the rights and obligations of the student.
6.9. Students who will go abroad within the framework of the Erasmus program are considered to be on leave for their
minor and double major education from different faculties during the period they are abroad and their rights are reserved.
6.10. Students continue to pay the contribution or tuition fee they are obliged to pay to GTU during the period they
study abroad. Students do not freeze their major program enrollment.
6.11. Repealed.
6.12. The University undertakes the necessary steps to ensure that students staying in dormitories affiliated with the
Higher Education Credit and Dormitories Institution retain their housing rights during their period abroad.
6.13. Students participating in the Erasmus exchange program are required to submit their transcripts for each semester
they complete at the host university to GTU.
6.14. ECTS to GTU grade conversions are carried out by the relevant d ivision's executive board, based on the valu es
specified in the “GTU–ECTS Grade Conversion Table”.

6.16. The grades of the courses taken abroad by undergraduate students are converted to the grading system applied at
GTU and these courses are recorded in the transcript with their original titles and are included in the semester average
and general average. Courses for which credits are not transferred appear on the transcript with the corresponding GTU
grade. These courses appear on the transcript as transfer courses. At the beginning of the rele vant semester, the name
and country of the university where the student studied this semester is indicated.
6.17. Failed courses taken in accordance with the learning agreement are recorded as FF in the GTU Student
Information System. Courses that do not have a grade on the transcript and cannot be documented as unsuccessful are
recorded as NA in the GTU Student Information System.
6.18. Graduate students may take the equivalent of Seminar or Thesis Study Course at the host university. In order for
students to take the approved equivalent of the Thesis Study Course abroad, they must have determined their thesis
topics at GTU.
6.19. The grades of the courses taken abroad by graduate students are converted to the grading system applied at GTU,
and these courses are recorded in the transcript with their original titles and are included in the semester average and
general average. Courses for which credits are not transferred also appear on the transcript with the corresponding GTU
grade. At the beginning of the relevant semester, the name and country of the university where the student studied this
semester is indicated.
6.20. Graduate students who will submit thesis proposals, thesis progress reports , or their thesis/dissertation must
complete the related procedures within 1 month from the end date of their study period as specified in the Confirmation
Letter, regardless of the academic calendar deadlines. Doctoral students who have taken the Doctoral Qualifying Exam
and failed on their first attempt are not eligible to parti cipate in the Erasmus exchange program during the period in
which they exercise their second attempt.
6.21. Staff members participating in training/teaching mobility are required to submit a Confirmation Letter at the end
of their activity. No grant payment will be made to those who fail to submit this document, and any payments already
made are refunded.
6.22. The mobility of undergraduate students participating in traineeship mobility is recognized with the decision of the
Faculty Executive Board. The mobility of graduate students participating in traineeship mobility is recognized with the
Confirmation Letter to be sent by the Coordinat ion Office to the Directorate of Student Affairs and recorded in the
explanatory notes section of the diploma supplement.
6.23. According to the approved Learning Agreement, a graduate student who takes the equivalent of the Thesis Study
course at the host institution may submit a "Thesis Study Equivalence Document" instead of a transcript at the end of
the semester, if the host institution does not provide a transcript for the course in question.
6.24. If the transcript submitted by the student includes the term "Pass" instead of a letter grade for a course, it will be
considered equivalent to an AA during grade conversion. Similarly, if the term "Fail" appears instead of a letter grade,
it will be considered equivalent to an FF.
Courses graded as "S/U" at GTU are not included in this scope.
6.25. In cases where a course taken from the institution of study according to the approved learning agreement
corresponds to more than one course, the grade received for this course is given to all related courses, provided that it
does not exceed GTU ECTS.
6.26. In cases where multiple courses correspond to a single course at GTU, if all of the courses are passed, the weighted
average of their grades is assigned to the equivalent course. However, if the student fails any of the courses taken in
place of a single course, the corresponding course at GTU is recorded as an FF in the GTU Student Information System.
The successfully completed courses are recorded as non -credit courses in accordance with Article 27(c) of the
Undergraduate Regulation.
6.27. The courses that graduate students take from the host institution during their study mobility are counted towards
a maximum of 3 (three) of the courses they are required to complete at GTU (excluding seminar and thesis study
courses).

Cases Without Provision
Article 7 - For matters not covered by this Directive, the provisions of the Gebze Technical University
Undergraduate/Graduate Education-Teaching and Exam Regulations, as well as the Erasmus+ Program Guide prepared
by the Center for European Union Education and Youth for each project period, shall apply.
Repealed Legislation
ARTICLE 8 – The “GTU Continuing Learning Program Erasmus Directive,” discussed and adopted at the University
Senate meeting dated 23/08/2011, session no. 2011/06, has been repealed.
Enforcement
ARTICLE 9- This Directive enters into force on the date of its adoption by the University Senate.
Execution
ARTICLE 10- The provisions of this Directive shall be executed by the Rector of GTU.
